events.title: Hormuz vessel attack and Saudi East-West pipeline disruption intensify fuel-cost risk for Taiwan airlines
observed_evidence: Reuters reported on 2026-09-13 that a projectile struck a vessel in the Strait of Hormuz, causing a fire and crew evacuation.
Reuters also reported that Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline had been temporarily shut after a drone attack; the route had become a key alternative while Hormuz traffic was heavily disrupted.
A separate Reuters report published 2026-09-12 said Houthi forces had tightened control around the Bab el-Mandeb/Red Sea chokepoint, adding a second major maritime-energy transit risk.

Taiwan's aviation fuel surcharge mechanism can offset only part of fuel-cost changes; Taiwan reporting earlier in 2026 documented that China Airlines, EVA Airways and STARLUX continued absorbing material portions of incremental fuel costs after surcharges.
events.semantic_interpretation: This is a material negative operating-cost catalyst for Taiwan passenger airlines because simultaneous pressure on Hormuz, Saudi bypass infrastructure and Red Sea transit raises the probability of sustained crude/jet-fuel and insurance/logistics cost pressure. The event does not establish a deterministic EPS or margin change; downstream production systems must validate actual fuel prices, hedging, surcharge recovery and company-specific exposure before modifying any valuation input.
events.raw_fetch_reason: Persist and hash the cited Reuters/Taiwan supporting pages where legally accessible, record canonical URLs and publication timestamps, and validate current company-specific fuel surcharge/hedging exposure before any production promotion.
